About this file

What it is. One file with everything in it: the courier box, the strip, the gift box, its sleeve, the lid, the ticket, the sounds, the music and five ways to play. It loads nothing from outside.

The reveal. The file starts as the person who received the gift sees it: a dark stage, the words "For name", "name sent you a gift" and "Something beautiful is waiting for you.", and a gold button that asks for a tap. The tap (or Enter, or five and a half seconds) brings the cover: a thick cloth that unrolls in front of the gift. A finger drawn across it parts it where the finger passes; sticky threads hold the two sides for a moment; what no longer hangs from the top falls, so a corner cut off is just that corner. When about a third is left hanging, the rest lets go. Once the cover is down, Skip, Enter or Space take it away too. Then two lamps swing onto the box. The two round buttons at the bottom turn each lamp off and on, and the box and its foil are lit by the lamps that are on. The page sets the names with window.EW_GIFT = { to: 'Alex', from: 'Sam' } or ?to=Alex&from=Sam in the address. ?reveal=0 (or window.EW_REVEAL = false) gives the plain unboxing on white, as on a product page. The event giftbox:revealed is sent to the window when the lamps are on.

How it goes. Turn the courier box over (it turns end over end, all the way round, and lies down on each of its four sides) until the tear strip is at the front, pull the strip, pull the sleeve off the gift box, lift the lid, take the ticket, scan it. If nothing is touched for a while, help comes in steps: a twinkle, a ring to put the finger on, a ghost finger that shows the way, and last a line of words. The six stars on top fill in as the steps are done. The round button with the arrow goes one step back (the ticket in, the lid shut, the sleeve on, back into the courier box, back onto its bottom); B on the keyboard does the same, R starts again from the beginning.

The ticket. It never comes out by itself. Tap it, pull it out of its pocket with the finger, or press T. While it is pulled its free end lifts and it bows like stiff card; when it comes free it springs flat. In front of you: drag it to tilt it, squeeze its two ends with two fingers to bend it, tap it to put it back, tap its square to scan.

Zoom. Two fingers, or Ctrl and the wheel, or the plus and minus keys, up to 50 times (the plus button up to 30 times). A double tap goes back to the whole picture. Magnified, the star print of the gift box and of the courier box is drawn by its own rule, so its borders stay sharp and the points of the stars meet; colour, light and paper stay those of the photos.

Sound. The switch at the right end of the top bar turns all sound off and on; the note next to it turns the music off and on. Both are on at the start. A browser starts sound only when a finger has lifted from the screen for the first time (or a key or a mouse button was pressed): that is what the first tap is for, and until then nothing is played or kept waiting. The music holds its breath while the cover is up, lifts when it falls and gains a layer with every step. "Choose the sounds" holds four kinds for every movement.

The ending. After the scan nothing flies into the square: four gold corners close in on it, light breaks out of it and the picture goes white; on the white a tick draws itself with the word "Unwrapped." and six stars. Then, by default, everything closes again and the "Add to cart" button of the page lights up (here: a stand-in card). The page can set another ending before this file's script runs: window.EW_FINISH = { mode: 'url', url: '...' } opens a web address; { mode: 'cart', cart: 'css selector' } names the page's own button. The event giftbox:scanned is sent to the window in any case.

Built-in test. Opened with ?qa=full at the end of its address, the file tests itself: it walks through every step, checks its own rules in every frame, shows coloured dots where a finger has to go and judges whether the touch did the right thing. Visitors never see it. The kinds are full, short, tablet, landscape and desktop.

Typefaces. The words of the reveal are set in Gelasio and Lexend, the two typefaces of the brand book. Both are carried inside this file under the SIL Open Font License 1.1 (Gelasio: copyright 2022 The Gelasio Project Authors; Lexend: copyright 2019 The Lexend Project Authors).

Sizes. The courier box is drawn from photos of the real one; its sizes (239,5 x 155,5 x 62 mm) are those of the earlier model, not the maker's. The white label under the real box is left out. The ticket shows a placeholder where the real one carries its number.
